algorithm: canonical / content_hash / section_digests: exactly as the 0.3 set (../manifest.json). digest: playbook_engine.digest.build_digest_v5(input) with the default token_budget, which for opf_version 0.6 is build_digest_v5 (OPF-SPEC.md §3.12.2): signed variants, refused asks and changed openings grouped by the grouping key of OPF-SPEC.md §3.5.4 (precedent.normalize_variant_text: every Counterparty-<n> alias -> 'counterparty', then deviation_classifier.normalize_for_standard with the document's perspective.party as the one party name -> 'party'), text = observation_builder.summarize_clause_text of the group representative; the signed variants labelled equivalent (vs_standard) collapse into one entry and the cap applies after collapsing. manifest / dossiers / provenance_index: playbook_engine.dossiers.build_derived_sections(input) (OPF-SPEC.md §3.12.3).

vectors.name: minimal-no-perspective
vectors.description: Smallest well-formed OPF 0.6 document: evidence {clauses: [], precedent: []}, no top-level perspective. expected.digest pins the digest_version 5 skeleton — perspective is PRESENT and null (never omitted), agreement_type is {id, name}, corpus counts are 0 and first_signed/last_signed are null, uncovered_clause_types is an empty list.

vectors.name: variants-refused-and-exclusions
vectors.description: One clause, eight deals, pinning digest_version 5 grouping and every exclusion rule: two deals signed our standard (n_signed_standard 2, never a variant); variant A signed in three deals, one spelled with different case/punctuation (exact normalization merges it) — its representative is the deal with the latest signed_on, a YYYY-MM month that sorts before every day in it (and whose digest first_signed / last_signed are 2025-03 and 2025-11); variant B differs from A by the negator 'not' only and stays a separate group; an unsigned deal's text is never a signed variant; a deal whose standard was struck (signed_text null, opening_text set) contributes no variant. The same refused ask in three deals (three spellings) is one group with n_deals 3 whose representative is the earliest-round ask. perspective is copied into the digest.

vectors.name: cap-totals-and-summary
vectors.description: One clause with seven distinct signed variants: the digest lists the top 5 (n_deals desc, last_signed desc with unknown last, then normalized text) and n_variants_total reports all 7. The two-deal variant's text exceeds 300 characters, pinning the sentence-boundary summary (a verbatim prefix ending on a sentence end, <= 300 chars). our_standard is null.

vectors.name: party-alias-grouping
vectors.description: The grouping key's party neutralization (OPF-SPEC §3.5.4): every entity-registry alias (Counterparty-<n>, case-insensitive, on word boundaries) becomes the token 'counterparty' and the document's perspective.party becomes the token 'party' before case and punctuation are dropped. Two deals whose signed texts differ only by the counterparty alias (Counterparty-2 vs Counterparty-5) are one variant with n_deals 2, and two refused asks that differ only by alias are one group with n_deals 2. The same words with the parties' places swapped stay a separate variant (our party and the counterparty are distinct tokens). The order of the two one-deal variants pins the perspective.party rewrite: 'notice of termination given to party ...' sorts before 'party may terminate ...'.

vectors.name: opening-evidence
vectors.description: Opening evidence (OPF-SPEC §3.5.5): opened_with and opening_text for seven deals of one clause. deal-a opened with our standard and signed an edit (opening_text = the standard); deal-b opened non-standard and signed our standard (opening_text recorded whatever its origin); deal-c opened non-standard and signed it unchanged (opened_with non_standard, opening_text null); deal-d added the clause in round 2 (opened_with absent, opening_text null); deal-e is unsigned (opened_with and opening_text null); deal-f's only edit is case (same grouping key, so opening_text null); deal-g opened non-standard and struck it before signing (opening_text set, signed_text null, no refused ask). The digest projects it as n_opened_standard 2 (deal-a, deal-f) / n_kept_standard 1 (deal-f), one signed variant (deal-a, -c, -d) carrying n_from_standard 1 and n_unchanged 1 (deal-d's absent clause counts in neither), and two changed openings (deal-b's, which ended at our standard, and deal-g's struck one).

vectors.name: opening-rules
vectors.description: The digest 5 opening rules (OPF-SPEC §3.12.2) on one clause with ten deals. n_opened_standard counts signed deals whose opened_with is standard (deal-a's edited standard, deal-b's struck standard, deal-i's kept one) and n_kept_standard those that signed our standard (deal-i only). Variants carry n_from_standard (deal-a conceded the New York variant from our standard) and n_unchanged (deal-d signed its non-standard opening as proposed); deal-g's 'absent' clause counts in neither. changed_openings: deal-c's non-standard opening that ended at our standard and deal-j's respelling of it are ONE entry (n_deals 2, n_to_standard 1); deal-f's struck opening with no refused ask is included (n_struck 1); deal-e's struck opening is also one of its own refused asks, so it is shown as a refused ask only; deal-h is unsigned and ignored.

vectors.name: equivalence-label-and-coverage
vectors.description: The vs_standard label in the digest (OPF-SPEC §3.5.6, §3.12.2) and uncovered_clause_types. Signed variants labelled equivalent (three deals, two distinct texts; the respelled text merges under the grouping key) collapse into ONE entry with n_deals 3, n_texts 2, two exemplars and the concession count; the rest are listed individually in tier order: less_protective (two deals), different_concept, the unjudged one (a signed text with no label), more_protective, then the collapsed entry. Each judged entry carries its part map (one token per part of our one-part standard), its addition tokens and its reason (issue #243); the unjudged one carries nulls. positions counts signed deals by standard, each label and unjudged. The refused ask and the changed opening carry their labels (the changed opening is mixed: its one part less protective, an addition more protective). The taxonomy lists one covered entry, an active and a custom entry with no evidence (uncovered_clause_types, sorted by taxonomy_id) and an inactive entry (never listed).

vectors.name: hard-rules-and-dossiers
vectors.description: The hard-rule manifest, the critic dossiers and the provenance index (OPF-SPEC §3.12.3). The Floor has seven invariants and the manifest seven rules in Floor order: venue-holds names clause.venue and carries a required_phrases condition, required_presence true and a permissible proof, with fallback_language the clause's standard; venue-no-arbitration states none of them (required_presence false, condition judged, no proof); term-cap names clause.term, which has no standard (fallback_language null), with a numeric_bound condition; survival-reference names clause.survival (a rule that demands presence or carries a predicate must name its clause) and carries a cross_reference condition with required_presence true; survival-scope and survival-period are two long judged rules on clause.survival; no-ghost-clause names a clause with no evidence (clause_id null). The venue dossier selects two excerpts from five candidate groups: first the concession on record (deal-a opened with our standard and signed the New York variant, although the Texas variant has more deals), then the first changed opening (deal-d's Oregon opening, which ended at our standard); its refused asks are not reached. It lists both Floor rules. No text is ever cut part-way. The term dossier (no standard, so a 1,000-token budget) selects two excerpts; its first, a long signed text, alone exceeds the budget and is kept whole; the second (deal-e's) is dropped whole and named (n_omitted 1, omitted_precedent_ids), then its Floor rule term-cap is dropped whole (n_floor_rules 1, none listed), since it is still over budget: a dossier holding its single kept excerpt is the only one that may exceed its budget. The survival dossier has a standard, no excerpt and three Floor rules that together exceed its budget, so the last listed (survival-period) is dropped whole and it fits (n_floor_rules 3, two listed). The assignment dossier pins how a group's record is chosen and a refused-ask excerpt: first the concession, deal-b's own opening-to-signed pair, although deal-a, which signed the same variant as proposed, is the lower document and precedent id (step 1 takes only members that opened with our standard); then, with no changed opening and the variant's group already chosen, the refused ask made in deal-c, deal-d and deal-f: deal-d and deal-f share the latest signed_on and deal-f has the lower precedent_id (deal-c has the lowest, but signed earlier; deal-d is the lower document), so the excerpt is deal-f's ask with what it signed instead (outcome ask_refused). Every deal but deal-f records source-file hashes and the corpus carries their snapshot hash: the provenance index repeats the hash and lists each excerpt deal's version_files (empty for deal-f). Its per-clause rows are in selection order, each marked omitted false or true: the term dossier's dropped excerpt is a row with omitted true that resolves to deal-e, which no kept excerpt cites, and deal-e is listed in documents for it.

vectors.name: standard-parts-and-owner-label
vectors.description: A standard of four parts whose second and fourth parts are the same passage (OPF-SPEC §3.5, §3.5.6, §3.12.2, §3.12.3, issue #243). The fourth part's part_id is the second's content hash with -2 appended, and the digest's our_standard carries all four parts in order. Every part map has one token per part, in standard order. Deal-a opened with our standard and signed a mixed variant (=, x0, -, = plus a more protective addition): a concession, the first signed variant, and the dossier's first excerpt, whose part_reasons name only the third part. Deal-b signed a variant that drops both copies of the repeated passage as neutral omissions: still equivalent, so it collapses (n_texts 1). Deal-c's refused ask keeps the first part, drops the rest (the third less protective) and adds a less protective sentence: less_protective. Deal-d opened with language whose parts derive mixed (-, x+, =, +) but the owner set the label to more_protective with a reason (owner_label): its changed opening in the digest carries label more_protective, label_by owner and the owner's reason, never the judgment's own reason, with the part map as judged; every other judged entry carries no label_by (its label is derived from its parts, the default the legend states) and the judgment's reason. The dossier's second excerpt is that changed opening, with label_by owner, the owner's reason and part reasons for the first, second and fourth (repeated, -2) parts.

vectors.name: signing-dates
vectors.description: When each deal was signed, as a fact (OPF-SPEC §3.8, §3.12.2, issue #247). corpus.documents[].signed_on is an ISO date or, when only the month is known, a YYYY-MM; signed_on_basis says where it was read (document_text, signature_block, filename, file_metadata) and is null exactly when signed_on is. Deal-f is signed but no source states a date (null, null); deal-g has no executed copy (signed_version null) and so no date. Every precedent record carries its document's signed_on. Digest 5 reports first_signed / last_signed as YYYY-MM: on the corpus (2022-03, 2024-11), on the clause (the same span over its precedent records), on each signed variant (variant A, two deals, 2022-03 to 2023-07 - a month-only date sorts before every day in it), on the collapsed equivalent entry when there is one, and on each refused ask group (the ask refused in deals c and e is dated by those deals' records: 2023-09 to 2024-11, and deal-f's refused ask, from a signed deal with no date, adds none).

vectors.name: settled-outcomes
vectors.description: How settled each judged text's vs_standard is (OPF-SPEC §3.5.6, §3.12.2, §3.12.3, issue #248): derived from the judgment's basis and blind check, never stored on the evidence. Four signed variants and the collapsed equivalent entry, in tier order: a mixed text the check disagreed on and a fresh agent decided (settled adjudicated), a less_protective text whose check agreed (agreed), a different_concept text whose check disagreed and still awaits adjudication (read as unchecked: nothing is settled yet), a more_protective text the owner set (owner; basis owner carries no check). The four equivalent texts collapse into one entry whose settled_counts is 2 agreed, 1 adjudicated, 0 unchecked, 1 owner, summing to n_texts 4; it carries no settled of its own. Of the two refused asks one is adjudicated and one is not judged (settled null); the one changed opening was never checked (unchecked). Each judged digest entry carries settled beside its label and part map, part_map_legend.settled states the four values, and the dossier's two excerpts (the concession whose judgment was adjudicated, the changed opening that was unchecked) carry settled in their vs_standard.

vectors.name: prior-standards
vectors.description: Our former forms and the standard history (OPF-SPEC §3.5.7, §3.12.2, issue #249). Three forms are supplied (baseline.prior_templates, with the content address and any dates the owner gave). Five of six deals' clauses opened on something of ours or a counterparty's: deal-a and deal-d opened on the 2018 form and signed it as it stood (opened_with prior_standard, opened_with_form 2018 form, no distinct opening_text: kept), deal-b opened on it and moved to today's standard (opening_text recorded, standard true), deal-c opened on the 2019 form and ended on a variant (conceded), deal-e opened with today's standard, and deal-f opened with the counterparty's own text (non_standard). The clause counts n_opened_prior 4, n_kept_prior 2 and n_moved_to_current 1 are derived from those records, and n_changed_openings is 1: only deal-f's opening is a counterparty ask, our own former wording never is. Each form's clause is judged once against today's two parts (role prior_standard, the same cache key as any text): the 2018 form's judgment is also the verdict of the two deals that signed its words. The 2021 form reads exactly as today's standard, so it is unchanged with no part map. The digest's standard_history lists the forms in config order with their in-use dates (config for the 2018 form, the config start and the latest signing month of its deals for the 2019 form: mixed, only the config start for the 2021 form), the opened, kept, conceded and moved-to-current deals, the part map against today's standard, and the form's own parts (null where the passage is today's); why_changed is the owner's note, the only reason ever given. Each form's clause is cited in that form's own bytes (document_id prior_template:<label>, version prior_template, resolved through the form's baseline.prior_templates sha256), never as template, which is today's form.

vectors.name: reconstructed-prior-form
vectors.description: A former form of ours rebuilt from the corpus when none was supplied (OPF-SPEC §3.5.7, issue #250). baseline.prior_templates holds one entry with basis reconstructed, n_deals 3 and the signing-month span of the deals that opened on it (first_signed 2020-02, last_signed 2021-03); it has no sha256 and no owner dates because it has no file. Three of four deals' clauses opened on it (opened_with prior_standard, opened_with_form the label): deal-a and deal-c signed it as it stood (kept), deal-b moved to today's standard; deal-d opened with today's standard. The prior standard's source_ref is the ordinary citation of the dominant wording in a corpus document (deal-a, version 3), never prior_template. The digest's standard_history form carries basis reconstructed and in-use dates inferred from the deals' signing months (in_use_basis deal_dates).

vectors.name: verified-absence
vectors.description: Verified absence counts (OPF-SPEC §3.5.8, §3.12.2, issue #251): evidence.absence has one record for every signed deal and clause type with no signed text, split into absent_verified and possibly_present, and the digest counts them per clause (n_signed_without_verified, n_signed_without_possible) and lists the verified deals (verified_absent_deals, latest signed_on first, undated last). The records are the output of the reference scorer over the deals' signed-text nodes: every node of a signed copy not filed under the clause is counted in n_checked, and a node filed under the clause that is too short to be precedent scores 1.0. Two clauses (assignment, governing law), eight deals. deal-a signed both clauses and is counted by neither; deal-g has no executed copy and is in no count. Assignment: deal-b (one node examined, its governing law clause, nothing close), deal-c (seven unclassified passages, none close), deal-f (opened with our standard and struck it before signing: it still signed without the clause; one node examined, its governing law clause) and deal-h (three nodes) are verified absent (n_signed_without_verified 4); deal-d has an unclassified passage scoring 0.308 against the clause and a passage the classifier filed under a third clause type (subcontracting) scoring 0.133 (a missed classification, so possibly present, candidates best first, each saying what the classifier filed it under, filed_under) and deal-e's executed copy yielded no nodes at all (basis unverifiable, possibly present, nothing checked): n_signed_without_possible 2. Governing law: deal-c and deal-d (whose five nodes score below the guard for this clause) are verified absent, ordered latest signed_on first (deal-d's month-only 2025-04 is after deal-c's 2025-03-10); deal-e is unverifiable and deal-h has a node the classifier assigned to the clause that was too short to be precedent (score 1.0, filed_under the clause itself), so possibly present. A node filed under the clause that is long enough to be precedent gives its deal a signed text and no absence record, so no record here cites one. The guard (0.1) is carried in evidence.absence.guard; a candidate scores at least that, and a scored record is absent_verified exactly when it has no candidate.
